solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Italian dish found a little way into the dictionary?

definitions.text: Italian dish found a little way into the dictionary?

parts.words: Italian dish found a little way into the dictionary?
parts.note: the whole clue invites splitting the dish's name in two, giving a position a short way beyond where an alphabetical list starts

explanation.surface: A cook reaches for the dictionary to look up a favourite Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as PAST A: a word found just after the A section begins would be a little way into any dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti, penne and their relatives are the classic staple food of Italian cooking.

clue.text: Painter's picture: a ship on top of ocean

parts.note: pic is a casual short form of picture
SS stands for steamship
O is the standard abbreviation for ocean on maps

explanation.surface: A painting shows a ship riding the waves of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on top of' simply places the pieces in order, the ship above the ocean letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish artist behind Cubism and Guernica.

clue.text: Insult with impact one has to countenance?

definitions.meaning: a snub or affront that wounds someone's pride
taken literally, a blow landing on the cheek, the face being one's countenance

explanation.surface: Someone is insulted and must simply put up with the sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countenance' looks like the verb 'tolerate', but the second reading uses the noun: the face.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a humiliating rebuff, from the literal smack on the cheek.

clue.text: It is a real crackpot that would be a trapeze artist

indicators.note: crackpot means crazy, so the words beside it are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a mad scheme as something only a circus performer could manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackpot' rearranges ITISAREAL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerialist performs high above the ring, on the trapeze or tightrope.

clue.text: Shellfish at sea? British tucking in with hesitation

indicators.note: the British letter is tucked into the middle of the word for being at sea

parts.note: at sea means confused, lost
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A Briton hesitantly tucks into a seafood dish while at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' looks like a location for the shellfish but means LOST; 'tucking in' puts B inside it to give LOBST.
explanation.definitionFit: The lobster is a large clawed marine crustacean, a classic shellfish.

clue.text: A Parisian engaged in flimsy, crazy thinking

indicators.note: one piece is engaged, or held, inside the other

parts.note: lacy fabric is delicate and flimsy
un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman is caught up in some flimsy, wild idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Parisian' is French for 'a'; 'engaged in' says it sits inside the flimsy word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunacy is madness or extreme foolishness, the state of thinking crazily.

clue.text: Dreadful book promotion?

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: A publisher's campaign for a book is judged terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad and dreadful both mean of very poor quality.

clue.text: Demand for 16 possibly producing incredulous expression

definitions.meaning: a child asking for another bedtime story, the answer to 16 across
said to someone whose tale you do not believe

explanation.walkthrough: 16 is the across answer BEDTIME STORY: a child after one story wants another.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock idiom of disbelief, and also a literal request for one more tale.

clue.text: Staff seen around a street

indicators.note: the staff is seen wrapped around the single letter

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Someone with a walking stick is spotted wandering about a street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' puts ROD round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Road and street are both public ways for traffic, synonyms in everyday use.

clue.text: Exasperation when serving tea with a smile

parts.note: cha (or char) is slang for tea
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: A waiter hides irritation while serving tea with a forced smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is annoyance or vexation at being disappointed or humiliated.

clue.text: Fourth in order took first place, backed by cheers

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the verb for leading is read backwards

parts.note: led means was in front, took first place
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A runner placed fourth recalls once leading, to cheers from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses LED to DEL; 'Fourth in order' looks like the race result but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Favourable slant by nearly all newspaper piece — and backbone

parts.note: spin is a favourable slant put on news

indicators.note: nearly means almost all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
a column is a regular newspaper article

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist puts a positive spin on nearly every story, showing some backbone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinal column is the vertebral column, literally the backbone.

clue.text: Secure team bagging 50 in big victory

parts.note: to land is to secure, as in land a deal

indicators.note: the team bags, or holds, the number within it

parts.note: a side is a team
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A cricket team scores 50 to secure a big win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bagging' puts L inside SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is an overwhelming win, especially in an election.

clue.text: Get old school guy with money to entertain area

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the money holds the area letter

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A wealthy former pupil gets someone in to host a local event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to entertain' puts A inside TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Relatives? Legally sons

parts.note: in law means legally

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether sons count as relatives in the legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In-laws are family members by marriage, such as a spouse's parents.

clue.text: Dodgy lawyer retiring — rest regrouping

parts.note: retiring means shy

indicators.note: regrouping means putting into a new arrangement, so the word beside it is jumbled

explanation.surface: A crooked lawyer retires and takes a rest to regroup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like stopping work but means SHY; 'regrouping' rearranges REST to STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is an unscrupulous lawyer, one using underhand methods.

clue.text: Here's politician before supporting a current measure

indicators.note: in a down clue what supports sits beneath, so the politician comes under the single letter

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A politician stands up to say he backs a current policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts MP below A in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the SI unit for measuring electric current.

clue.text: What might you tell children about to go out?

definitions.text: What might you tell children about to go out?

parts.words: What might you tell children about to go out?
parts.note: 'go out' suggests leaving the house, but here it means dropping off to sleep, as children do after a tale at night

explanation.walkthrough: 'go out' looks like heading outdoors; it means falling asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale read aloud to a child at night, just before they sleep.

clue.text: Upset crazy attempt

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A frustrated person is upset by a mad try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses BATS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab is an informal word for a try, as in have a stab at it.

clue.text: Heading for this lake to catch raw fish

indicators.note: the outer letters catch, or enclose, the middle word
the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An angler heads for a lake hoping to catch fish to eat raw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for' takes T from this; T and L 'to catch' RAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To trawl is to fish by dragging a net behind a boat.

clue.text: Item at auction offering good deal?

definitions.meaning: an item put up for sale at auction
a great amount, a good deal

explanation.definitionFit: An auction lot is a sale item, while a lot also means plenty.

clue.text: Core material in support of golfer recalled in well-chosen words

indicators.note: in places the core material inside the reversed support
recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball, so it serves the golfer
pith is the soft core material of a plant

explanation.surface: A golfer delivers a few choice words after a tee shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns the golfer's support round to EET, and 'in' sets the core material inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive phrase or apt name for someone, a chosen label.

clue.text: Inhale and swim round about

indicators.note: the swim word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to bathe is to swim
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A swimmer takes a breath and does another lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the swim word about the short Latin-derived 're' meaning about.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhale is to breathe in; the answer covers drawing in air.

clue.text: Panic, losing head? That's a mistake

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: terror is panic or extreme fear

explanation.surface: Someone warns that panicking and losing your head is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops T from TERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a slip or blunder, a plain synonym.
